title: ingest-rate-normalizer-with-graceful-tenant-throttling
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Console metrics ingest occasionally experiences short, high-amplitude spikes from customer tenants (large dev loops, CI bursts, or customer-side misconfiguration). These spikes blow past our admission-control windows, causing cascading queue growth, increased CPU on enrichment workers, and p95/p99 latency regressions for other tenants.

Goal: Implement an ingest-side 'rate normalizer' that smooths short bursts per-tenant and provides graceful degradation instead of a hard drop. The normalizer should preserve high-value signals (errors, rollouts, billing-critical counters) while reducing noise (high-cardinality debug events, verbose SDK heartbeats) during spikes. This should protect downstream processors and provide predictable SLOs for the console UX.

Proposed design (high level):
- Per-tenant adaptive windowed coalescer: short-term rolling windows (100ms/500ms/2s tiers) that can coalesce similar events (same metric name + small label subset) into aggregated deltas. Windows chosen based on observed burst characteristics per tenant.
- Priority-based shedding rules: events tagged as critical (error, billing, quota) are never coalesced; low-priority events are aggregated or sampled aggressively during a spike.
- Token-bucket burst budget per tenant (leaky-bucket style) that allows normal bursts but throttles sustained spikes above baseline. The budget is dynamic and learns a tenant's normal rate over a 24h window.
- Graceful degradation paths: when shedding is triggered, emit aggregated 'dropped_event' telemetry that includes sampling ratios so downstream consumers and dashboards can reconstruct approximate counts.
- Feedback signals to clients and Console: emit per-tenant metrics (ingest_budget_usage, coalesced_rate, shed_rate) and surface in Console Observability so customers/operators can see and request quota increases.
- Fast-apply policy engine: allow rules per-customer tiers (free vs paid vs enterprise) and emergency overrides via Console rollout config.

Implementation plan:
1) Library: implement a lightweight in-process coalescer + per-tenant token bucket in the ingress gateway (Node/Go layer depending on gateway). Keep it single-threaded per-shard to avoid cross-shard coordination.
2) Metrics & telemetry: instrument budget usage, window occupancy, coalesced_event_count, and dropped_event_aggregates. Add tracing spans for events that get coalesced or shed.
3) Config: add mutable runtime config in the control plane (per-tenant policies, global thresholds). Default policies derived from pilot telemetry.
4) Load testing: create synthetic high-cardinality tenants that replay real burst traces; compare p50/p95/p99 and CPU across baseline vs normalizer.
5) Rollout: canary on internal tenants -> 10% production shards -> 50% -> global. Provide quick rollback toggle.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Coalescing introduces short windows where exact event timestamp ordering is lost; we add aggregated timestamps and counts to mitigate analytics fidelity loss.
- Sampling and shedding reduce raw telemetry fidelity; mitigated by tagging aggregates with sampling_rate and providing customers the ability to disable shedding for critical routes (enterprise feature).
- Learning per-tenant baselines adds state; we plan to store compact summaries and evict cold tenants after 24h to bound memory.

Observability and SLOs:
- Target: reduce cross-tenant p99 latency amplification during spikes by 60% in synthetic tests.
- Expose console-facing dashboard tiles: per-tenant budget_utilization, coalesced_event_rate, shed_rate, and per-route error impact.
- Add alerts: tenant_budget>90% for >1min, global_shed_rate>0.5% sustained.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Ingress+Rate+Normalizer+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-gateway/pull/2386
- Load test harness: https://perf.redwood.ai/job/ingest-normalizer-load-2025-02

Acceptance criteria:
- Integrations tests showing dropped_event_aggregates can reconstruct counts within 5% of baseline for high-volume metrics.
- Load test: when simulating a 10x burst for 1m, overall p99 for healthy tenants does not increase by more than 10% relative to steady-state.
- No unbounded memory growth with 100k tenants simulated (eviction policy effective).
- Runtime configurable and togglable via feature flag for rollback.

Next steps:
